title: 7-Zip won't update itself: fix this XZ archive bug tonight (CVE-2026-14266)
description:
7-Zip never updates itself, and older copies have a high-severity bug: CVE-2026-14266, a heap-based buffer overflow in how 7-Zip opens XZ archives. A booby-trapped file could let an attacker run code on your computer when you open it.

The US National Vulnerability Database (NVD) scores it 7.8 out of 10 (High); Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), which published the advisory, rates it 7.0. The fix is 7-Zip 26.02, released June 25, 2026. As of the July reports, there was no public proof-of-concept and no reported exploitation in the wild, and it is not on the US agency CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list.

Analyst note: the bigger risk is apps that never update, sitting on a PC for years. Programs that bundle 7-Zip's code need their own fix from their vendor; updating standalone 7-Zip does not cover them.

Do this tonight: open 7-Zip, then Help, then About. If it is older than 26.02, download the new version from 7-zip.org and run the installer.

Sources
- ZDI-26-444 advisory via oss-security (Jul 17, 2026): https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/07/17/12
- CVE-2026-14266 record (NVD/MITRE via OpenCVE): https://app.opencve.io/cve/CVE-2026-14266
- The Hacker News (Jul 20, 2026): https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/new-7-zip-vulnerability-could-let.html
- TechSpot: https://techspot.com/news/113175-7-zip-patches-flaw-could-run-malware-opening.html

Narration uses an AI voice (ElevenLabs). Research, script and fact-check by Securidge.
